answer: A bonded stake makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove it misbehaved. A single operator running a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand deposits, so the attack cost scales linearly instead of being free. Honest agents treat the stake as a haven for trust, while cheap copies wash away like shale in a river — the deposit is the filter that keeps the market honest.
